$comment: HARNESS-16 — the AI-review engine registry (PRD §3 ports doctrine applied to CI).
The review PORT is fixed and engine-agnostic: read a CODEOWNERS-protected reviewer
definition, diff the PR against its base, write a review whose last line is a
`VERDICT:` line. Every ADAPTER (engine) must satisfy exactly that contract, and the
verdict parse in ai-review.yml is the contract test that binds all of them equally —
an engine that cannot produce a parseable verdict fails as DID NOT COMPLETE rather
than being silently accepted.
TO SWAP THE REVIEWING MODEL: change `active` to another engine's key. That is the whole
change. Exactly one engine reviews, by construction — there is no way to enable two and
accidentally double the spend, which is the point. (Cross-checking with two engines was
deliberately dropped: it doubles cost for a check that is advisory anyway. Re-adding it
would be a considered control-plane change, not a config flag.)
TO ADD AN ENGINE: add an entry here AND a guarded adapter step in
.github/workflows/ai-review.yml between the ADAPTERS START/END markers. Doing only the
first fails the `config` job loudly (scripts/ai-review-matrix.mjs), before any token is
spent — a registry entry with no adapter would otherwise produce a leg that runs,
executes nothing, and reports the generic DID NOT COMPLETE.
This file is deliberately NOT overridable by a repository variable. Under HG-0006 the
reviewer prompts and the model serving them are model configuration, and HG-0002 puts
model configuration under control-plane-owners. An admin-settable override would move
part of that decision outside CODEOWNERS review — so changing which model reviews the
agent's work is a control-plane PR, by design.
FIELDS
active   key of the one engine that reviews. Must name a registered engine that has
an adapter step.
model    null means 'let the engine pick its own default' — used where pinning a
specific model id would mean inventing one not verified to exist.
secret   name of the Actions secret holding this engine's credential. Read generically
as secrets[matrix.engine.secret]; never hardcoded in the core. If the active
engine's secret is missing, preflight reports NOT RUN — loudly, and explicitly
not a pass — rather than silently reviewing nothing.
attribution  comment footer. Engine-specific on purpose: attributing a Codex review to
Claude Code would misstate which model produced the verdict.
requires_workflow_parity  true where the engine's own tooling refuses to run when this
workflow file differs from the default branch. That is claude-code-action's
anti-exfiltration rule (a PR must not be able to rewrite the workflow AND
obtain the app token), not a universal one — the CLI-based adapters use a
plain repository secret and have no such rule.
VERIFIED SURFACES (probed, not assumed — see docs/adrs/0029)
claude  anthropics/claude-code-action@v1, --model in claude_args. PROVEN in CI.
codex   @openai/codex v0.147.0 — `codex exec --model --sandbox --color`. RUN IN CI, AND
IT DOES NOT WORK AS WRITTEN. Auth is fine (CODEX_API_KEY, model gpt-5.6-sol,
14,443 tokens spent) but codex's own sandbox is bubblewrap, which cannot
initialise in the Actions runner: `bwrap: loopback: Failed RTM_NEWADDR`. That
fails at sandbox SETUP, so EVERY mode dies with it, read-only included — reads,
writes and a plain `pwd` all failed and no review file was written.
The only mode that runs is the no-OS-sandbox one, which is a SECURITY DECISION
FOR A HUMAN, not a config tweak, and is NOT applied here. Two costs: it removes
real containment against prompt injection carried in a reviewed diff, and codex
separately lacks the workflow-parity protection (see requires_workflow_parity
below) that stops a PR editing this workflow from running with the key.
DO NOT set active to codex until that decision is made deliberately.
gemini  @google/gemini-cli v0.55.1 — `gemini -p --model --approval-mode yolo
--skip-trust`; GEMINI_API_KEY confirmed read. --skip-trust is REQUIRED: without
it the CLI silently downgrades yolo to default and refuses to act. It EXITS 0
on both that refusal and on a critical API error — which is precisely why the
core never trusts an adapter's exit code and checks for the review file
instead. NEVER RUN END TO END.
